description: BREAK, CONTINUE, RETURN, RAISE, LET and NULL are SCRIPTING statements: legal inside a BEGIN...END block, and standing alone they are refused as syntax errors. THE POSITION IS THE OFFENDING TOKEN'S OWN, for all six alike - '   BREAK' reads position 3, a newline then two spaces then LET reads line 2 position 2 - and the word is echoed exactly as written, so a lower-case null is quoted in lower case. An earlier reading had five of them pinned at a constant line 1 position 0; that was the LIVE HARNESS trimming each statement's leading whitespace before submitting it, so the account was answering about text it had never been given. AFTER a complete query the same word is a different thing entirely: live parses 'SELECT x FROM t break' as a query with a bare ALIAS and runs it, and the alias resolves - a SEMICOLON is what makes it a statement again, and that one is refused at its own place. NULL is the exception among the trailing words: it is the literal, not a name, so it cannot alias anything. Converted 1:1 from procedures/StrayScriptingStatementTest (now retired).
